item.title: [10] Rotational Phonons Activated by Magnetism as a Key Ingredient of Cuprate Physics
item.description:
Last authors: Jianwei Sun, Ruiqi Zhang

Authors: Yanyong Wang, Manuel Engel, Christopher Lane, et al.

Score 10/10 A_MUST_READ

Why: Direct connection to ARPES, cuprates, electron-phonon coupling, and magnetic effects in unconventional superconductors.

Tags: #ARPES #cuprates #superconductivity #electron_phonon_coupling #DFT #magnetism #Hall_effect

Abstract: Circularly polarized lattice vibrations carry angular momentum and can link lattice dynamics to collective responses in strongly correlated materials, particularly cuprate superconductors. Angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (ARPES) reveals ubiquitous quasiparticle "kinks" near ~70 and ~40 meV in cuprates, often accompanied by peak-dip-hump (PDH) features, indicating strong coupling between electrons and low-energy bosonic excitations. However, the relevant phonon modes and the role of circularly polarized vibrations in these spectral anomalies remain largely elusive. Here, we investigate electron-phonon coupling (EPC) in hole-doped infinite-layer CaCuO2 at four selective hole dopings (12.5%-56.25%) using the Strongly Constrained and Appropriately Normed (SCAN) density functional with explicit magnetic interactions. At 25% doping, the magnetic phase exhibits substantially stronger EPC (lambda ~ 0.5), five times that of the nonmagnetic phase, producing kinks and PDH features over 40-80 meV, with self-energy magnitudes comparable to experiment. Oxygen rotational phonons dominate the coupling over 50-65 meV, while breathing modes play a lesser role; the rotational modes emerge exclusively in the magnetic phase. At 37.5% doping, lambda increases to ~1.6 due to strong coupling of low-frequency phonons near the Fermi-surface nesting wave vector, whereas at 56.25%, where Cu magnetic moments vanish, lambda decreases to ~0.4. The rotational modes carry staggered angular momentum that cancels in the unperturbed lattice; a time-reversal-breaking gyrotropic coupling on Cu sites lifts this cancellation, yielding a finite phonon thermal Hall conductivity. Our findings establish magnetism-enhanced EPC as an important ingredient of cuprate physics and identify rotational oxygen phonons as relevant to spectral anomalies, superconductivity, and the pseudogap thermal Hall effect.

item.title: [9] Kitaev Exchange and Altermagnetism in the Double Perovskite Sr2CoTeO6: An Ab Initio Study
item.description:
Last authors: Alexey V. Ushakov, Sergey V. Streltsov

Score 9/10 A_MUST_READ

Why: Ab initio prediction of altermagnetism and Kitaev exchange in a specific double perovskite material.

Tags: #material #altermagnetism #DFT

Abstract: The Co$^{2+}$-based double perovskite Sr$_2$CoTeO$_6$ attracts attention due to its nontrivial magnetic properties. \textit{Ab initio} density functional theory calculations reveal a substantial ferromagnetic Kitaev exchange $|K|\sim J/3$ between nearest neighbors that, combined with the face-centered cubic lattice, leads to pronounced exchange frustration and places Sr$_2$CoTeO$_6$ among Kitaev materials with moderate Kitaev interaction strength. In addition, Sr$_2$CoTeO$_6$ is found to be altermagnetic with a sizable non-relativistic spin splitting, which can give rise to a transverse piezomagnetic effect and a nontrivial magneto-optical response.

item.title: [9] Magnetic Reconfiguration Controls Spin Splitting and Spin-Orbit-Coupled Responses in Compensated Magnets
item.description:
Last authors: Zehao Ji, Qihang Liu

Authors: Yongqian Zhu, Lu Liu, Xiaobing Chen, et al.

Score 9/10 A_MUST_READ

Why: Investigates spin splitting and anomalous Hall in altermagnets and compensated magnets, a direct interest.

Tags: #altermagnetism #anomalousHalleffect #spinsplitting #DFT #magneticmaterials

Abstract: Compensated magnets provide a versatile platform for spin-dependent electronic and transport phenomena. Here, we show that magnetic reconfiguration, i.e., selective reversal of local moments without changing the underlying crystal structure, can profoundly transform the nonrelativistic spin splitting and spin-orbit-coupled responses of spin-degenerate antiferromagnets (AFMs), altermagnets (AMs), and compensated ferrimagnets (cFIMs). Strikingly, magnetic configurations with nearly degenerate energies can exhibit qualitatively different spin-split band structures and anomalous Hall responses, allowing a small magnetic-energy scale to produce large changes in physical properties. Combining tight-binding models, oriented spin space group analysis, and first-principles calculations, we demonstrate that converting an AM configuration into cFIM states activates staggered onsite-potential contributions to spin splitting, complementing the anisotropic-hopping mechanism of AMs and removing symmetry-enforced degeneracies. Moreover, cFIM symmetry permits an anomalous Hall response at first order in spin-orbit coupling, in contrast to the higher-order or orientation-constrained responses of corresponding AM states. We demonstrate this regime in Mn2Mo3O8, one of 12 cFIM candidates identified in the MAGNDATA database, and further demonstrate its generality by designing cFIMs from collinear AFMs, exemplified by MnGeO3 and Co2Mo3O8. Our results establish magnetic reconfiguration as a powerful symmetry-guided strategy for dramatically reshaping electronic and transport responses in compensated magnets.

item.title: [9] Quantum Geometric Origin of N\'eel-Order-Driven Magneto-Optical Response in MnTe
item.description:
Last authors: Daegeun Jo, Peter M. Oppeneer

Authors: Suman Rooj, M. S. Mrudul, Daegeun Jo, Peter M. Oppeneer

Score 9/10 A_MUST_READ

Why: Direct connection of altermagnetism, Berry curvature, N'eel order, and anomalous Hall effect via MO response and DFT.

Tags: #altermagnetism #Berrycurvature #anomalousHall #antiferromagnet #DFT #magneto-optics

Abstract: Magneto-optical (MO) responses provide a direct probe of magnetic order, yet resolving compensated antiferromagnetic order remains challenging. Here, we demonstrate in altermagnetic MnTe that the symmetry of the N\'{e}el order is imprinted on the MO response through distinct quantum-geometric contributions. Combining first-principles calculations with a Landau symmetry framework, we demonstrate that the quantum metric gives rise to a twofold optical anisotropy, with its diagonal and symmetric off-diagonal components forming an $E_{2g}$ doublet associated with the quadratic N\'{e}el-order invariants, providing a characteristic MO Voigt signature of the N\'{e}el-vector orientation. In contrast, the Berry curvature generates a complementary threefold Hall response governed by the cubic $A_{2g}$ N\'{e}el-order invariant. Although the Hall conductivity and the out-of-plane weak-ferromagnetic moment share the same symmetry and angular dependence, constraining the latter to zero leaves the optical Hall response essentially unchanged demonstrating that the Hall response originates directly from the compensated N\'{e}el order rather than the net magnetization. Our results establish quantum geometry as a direct link between N\'{e}el order and MO response, revealing distinct twofold and threefold optical signatures of N\'{e}el order in altermagnetic MnTe.

item.title: [9] Superconductivity from a Cooper surface instability in a nodal Bose metal
item.description:
Last authors: Jian-Jian Miao, Cui Ding

Score 9/10 A_MUST_READ

Why: Theoretical mechanism for unconventional superconductivity in cuprates, proposing experimental tests via photoemission and STS.

Tags: #superconductivity #cuprates #correlatedelectrons #Luttingerliquid #theory #photoemission #STS

Abstract: In underdoped cuprates, the superconducting gap is largest where low-energy electron spectral weight is already depleted above the transition. How can a weak attraction drive superconductivity when the one-electron density of states vanishes? In a momentum-space \(t\)--\(J\) model, the exactly solvable normal state is a nodal Bose metal with four one-electron nodes. Along two contours called Cooper surfaces, adding or removing a spin-singlet pair of electrons with opposite momenta costs no energy. The resulting logarithmic divergence of the pair susceptibility allows an arbitrarily weak pair-transfer attraction to stabilize a correlated nodal \(d\)-wave superconductor. Spin-resolved coincidence photoemission could test this pairing mechanism by resolving two zero-energy pair-removal ridges above the transition and a third along the underlying Luttinger surface below it.

item.title: [9] Transverse Shifts Driven by Geometric Orbital Torque in Altermagnets
item.description:
Last authors: Yugui Yao, Zhi-Ming Yu

Authors: Runze Li, Yugui Yao, Zhi-Ming Yu

Score 9/10 A_MUST_READ

Why: Predicts novel spin separation in altermagnets driven by orbital torque, a direct user interest.

Tags: #altermagnetism #spin-orbitcoupling #spinseparation #theory #magneticmaterials

Abstract: Anomalous transverse shifts in interface reflection are conventionally attributed to spin-orbit coupling or its pseudospin analogue. Here, we uncover a distinct geometric mechanism driven solely by an orbital torque arising from Fermi-surface anisotropy. During total reflection, an incident wave packet penetrates the anisotropic transmitted medium as an evanescent wave. There, the broken rotational symmetry about the interface normal exerts an orbital torque, and the accumulated angular impulse---the product of the torque and the dwell time---leads to a transverse spatial shift. Applying this mechanism to altermagnets without spin-orbit coupling, we show that the orbital torque is odd in spin. As a consequence, the two spin channels are deflected to opposite sides of the incident plane, giving an intrinsic spatial spin separation in altermagnets. The shift also inherits the angular symmetry of the altermagnetic spin splitting and is strongly enhanced near the onset of total reflection. Our work thus uncovers a new mechanism for transverse shifts, predicts a novel spin separation effect in altermagnets, and offers a direct probe of the altermagnetic order.
